evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社 / 遼寧人民出版社, 2012
evidence.field: 山部 entry; printed p. 810, PDF p. 823; continuation checked on printed p. 811, PDF p. 824
evidence.text: The entry identifies 山 as a pictograph of mountain peaks standing together. It describes Shang oracle-bone forms as showing mountain outlines, and Shang and Western Zhou bronze forms as varying between filled or outlined forms and three or five peaks. It describes subsequent stylization, gives the basic sense as a high, pointed part of the ground, and cites 《合集》96 and examples from the 詩經 and 荀子. The printed prose and cited forms checked match the provisional OCR; the entry ends on p. 810, with no continuation on p. 811.
evidence.title: CiNii 図書 — 字源

evidence.source: 香港中文大學漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; 山
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle-bone 山 as mountain peaks standing together, but cautions that 山 can be confused with 火 and says scholars distinguish them partly by inscription context. It reports oracle-bone uses in the mountain sense, including 《合集》20271 (“王陟山”), as a mountain deity in 《合集》30173 (“其求雨于山”), and in a personal name. It reports possible literal 山谷 in a bronze inscription, alongside place-name, clan-name and personal-name uses. These reported contexts do not establish a dated sequence of semantic developments.
evidence.kind: character-specific paleographic and usage database record
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析：山

evidence.source: 中央研究院 Academia Sinica, Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The record calls 山 a pictograph depicting mountain peaks standing together. It lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and 說文 forms and cites bronze references 集成05396 and 金文詁林索引9.245. Its text does not date every specimen or establish a continuous stroke-by-stroke derivation.
evidence.title: 漢字「山」：字形演變

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, 山部; online transcription with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.text: The transcription gives the historical dictionary account that 山 disperses qi, gives rise to things, is high and rocky, and is pictographic. Duan Yucai comments on the wording and notes a textual emendation for 𢿱. This documents a historical lexicographic interpretation; it does not independently prove the graph’s original formation or sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「山」

gaps: The reported early inscription examples are mediated through the CUHK database; the underlying oracle-bone records and a dated specimen were not independently inspected here. The exact lexical value of the earliest 山 graph therefore remains unresolved.

《字源》 prints 《合集》96 as “勿于九山寮?” with a tentative sacrificial gloss. The cited inscription and its interpretation were not independently checked against the underlying corpus; treat this as a question or attributed proposal, not a settled attestation.
The 《字源》 discussion cites 詩經 and 荀子 examples, but this research did not establish their composition dates or earliest physical witnesses.

The listed graphic stages and the 《字源》 account describe changes but do not establish a continuous stroke-by-stroke lineage across every specimen. No individual historical glyph image was used as evidence in this result.
No phonetic component or whole-graph phonetic-loan analysis is proposed for 山. No sequence of semantic extensions or graph borrowing was established here.
The official Unicode Unihan character record and full local readings table were not inspected in this invocation; no Unihan reading is claimed.
No scan or OCR correction is proposed: PDF p. 823’s 山 headword and passage were checked against the supplied scan, and PDF p. 824 was checked for an entry continuation.
